name: REVENTOR Calendar Appointment Booking
author: REVENTOR

sections.description:
REVENTOR Calendar Appointment Booking lets visitors book appointments on your WordPress site and keeps your own calendar (Nextcloud, Radicale, Baïkal, iCloud, Fastmail and other CalDAV servers) in sync — both ways.

Built around a simple promise: your booking data stays on your server, availability is always correct, and everything just works.

Highlights

  • Two-way CalDAV sync — bookings appear in your calendar with reminders, and busy events (including recurring ones, holidays, absences) block slots in the booking form. Tested against Nextcloud, Radicale and Baïkal.
  • Bookings stored in WordPress — a real appointments list with confirm/cancel, manual booking, CSV export, and sync status for every booking. Double bookings are prevented at the database level.
  • A booking widget people like using — a 3-step wizard with month calendar, clear time slots, clear states (“fully booked” is never confused with “temporarily unavailable”), dark mode, fully keyboard accessible. Works with page caches: availability always loads live.
  • Made to match your site — primary color, corner radius, density and custom CSS; the widget inherits your theme’s fonts. No forced design.
  • Emails that arrive — confirmation, admin notification and reminders are queued and retried, with an outbox log. ICS attachments included.
  • Private by design — no third-party service, consent checkbox, WordPress privacy exporter/eraser integration, CalDAV passwords encrypted at rest.
  • Free, without add-on fragmentation — unlimited calendars and services included.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open REVENTOR Booking in your admin menu. A starter calendar and service are created for you.
  3. Connect your CalDAV calendar: paste your server URL, enter your credentials (an app password is recommended), click Discover, and pick your calendar.
  4. Set your working hours and services, then place [reventor-calendar] on any page. For a specific calendar, use [reventor-calendar cal_2].

Upgrading from 1.x? Go to REVENTOR Booking → Tools — your settings and appointment types migrate in one click, and past bookings can be backfilled from your calendar.
sections.faq:
Which calendar servers are supported?

Any CalDAV server: Nextcloud, Radicale, Baïkal, iCloud, Fastmail, IONOS, mailbox.org and others. The connection test detects your server type and runs a real calendar query — so “connected” means connected.

Does it work with Google Calendar or Outlook?

Not natively yet — CalDAV is the focus of 2.0. Google Calendar and Microsoft 365 are planned for a later release.

Does it work with page caching plugins?

Yes. Availability is loaded live after page load, so WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache and friends can cache your pages aggressively without showing stale slots.

How are time zones handled?

Everything is stored in UTC and computed in your business timezone with proper DST handling. Times are shown in your business timezone with a clear label; visitors can optionally switch to their own timezone.

Can customers cancel or reschedule?

Planned for 2.1. For now you can cancel bookings from the admin, and the calendar stays in sync.
sections.changelog:
2.0.0

Complete rewrite of the plugin core.

  • Bookings are now stored in WordPress (the previous version only wrote to the calendar): appointments list, statuses, manual booking, CSV export.
  • CalDAV sync rebuilt from scratch: calendar discovery with a picker instead of URL pasting, recurrence (RRULE) expansion so recurring events and absences actually block slots, correct timezone handling including quoted TZID parameters and all-day events, race-safe event creation, and a retry queue so a calendar outage never blocks a booking.
  • Live calendar check: when a visitor picks a service and again right before a booking is stored, the plugin compares with the connected calendar using one small request (events are re-read only when the calendar changed), so appointments added moments ago block their slots immediately.
  • Fixed the reported issue where booked Nextcloud time slots still appeared as available; conflict checking now fails closed with visible errors instead of silently showing everything as free.
  • Updating from 1.x is safe: your settings keep working through a one-click migration (an admin notice guides you there), and booking stays closed on an unconfigured setup until it ran, so nothing is ever booked into a default calendar.
  • New booking widget: no jQuery, multi-instance, cache-proof live availability, accessibility (keyboard, screen reader, reduced motion), dark mode, timezone label with optional visitor toggle.
  • Email delivery moved to a queue with retries and an outbox log; ICS attachments generated safely in memory; reminder emails added (in addition to calendar VALARM reminders).
  • New admin area: dashboard with needs-attention list, calendars and settings with explicit save, holidays/vacation day overrides, tools with diagnostics, a one-click system report, and a 1.x migration.
  • Security hardening: capability checks everywhere (the 1.x anonymous CalDAV debug endpoint is gone), encrypted CalDAV passwords, server-side validation of every booking (no more past/outside-hours bookings via crafted requests), honeypot, time-trap and rate limiting.
  • Deactivating the plugin no longer deletes your settings; uninstall removes all customer data and, optionally, configuration.
